bugs.title: Newly created Shadow Clone repo is empty except for the sync marker file
bugs.notes: ROOT CAUSE FOUND against the live GitHub API (not from prior notes). Repro of the pre-fix code on this account PASSED (303 blobs) because this account's default-branch preference is 'main' — proving the prior sweep's 'verified' claim was true HERE but non-general. The real defect, confirmed by probing GitHub's actual behavior with fresh auto_init:false repos: an empty repo's default branch becomes whatever the FIRST-created branch is. bug-46's fix hard-coded DEFAULT_BRANCH ('main') for the bootstrap Contents-API PUT and the final ref PATCH. On an account whose default-branch preference is 'master' (or anything else), the bootstrap commit lands on refs/heads/master, GitHub makes MASTER the default branch, while the full-tree commit is PATCHed onto refs/heads/main — the repo's default view then shows only .clipforge-sync.json. That is exactly the reported symptom, and it is invisible to any verification done on a main-preference account. Also verified live during the fix: (1) default_branch can report the PLANNED name ('main') for ~1s after the first commit even when only refs/heads/master exists, so a single read-back is not trustworthy — the fix polls until the reported branch's ref actually exists; (2) POST /branches/<b>/rename moves refs instantly but updates default_branch ASYNCHRONOUSLY (1-3s lag, verified by polling), so the fix normalizes master->main with the synchronous sequence create refs/heads/main -> PATCH /repos {default_branch} -> DELETE refs/heads/master. FIX in createPrivateShadowClone (bot/src/github.js): bootstrap on target.default_branch from POST /user/repos; poll-until-settled read-back of the live default branch; PATCH the settled branch with the full-tree commit; normalize to 'main' synchronously when it differs; new post-conditions — the repo's default-branch head must equal the full-tree commit AND the pushed tree must contain >= copiedFiles blobs, else throw instead of reporting success on a sync-marker-only repo. VERIFIED end-to-end against the live GitHub API with fresh PAT-created repos: Phase A (normal account) 302 source files + sync marker on main, head commit 'Shadow clone from motionssalt/clipforge@524ec66', bot/src/github.js AND assets/anime_reference_color_cube_l8.png byte-identical to the source blobs; Phase B (simulated master-preference account executing the fixed algorithm step-for-step) poll settles to master, PATCH lands the full tree there, synchronous normalization flips default_branch to main, root listing immediately shows the full tree, master ref gone. Bot test suite: 110/110 pass (prior sweep's 5 unrelated failures no longer present). Fix commit a26467e, confirmed on origin/main.

bugs.title: No visible progress indicator while a Shadow Clone is being created
bugs.notes: IMPLEMENTED AND VERIFIED. bot/src/index.js handleClonePatMessage: immediately after the PAT message is deleted (§8.1.5), the already-acknowledged PAT prompt message is edited in place into an in-progress state ('Creating your Shadow Clone — this can take a minute — the bot is working.' + indeterminate 'Preparing repository…' bar) via the standard renderInteractiveView self-edit — instant feedback, no extra chat messages, no new messaging mechanism. Incremental progress: createPrivateShadowClone (bot/src/github.js) gained an optional third arg { onProgress({stage, done, total}) } reporting stages source -> copy (once per 4-file chunk) -> finalize; the handler renders 'Copying files… done/total' with the existing progress.js progressBar into the same status message, throttled to at most one edit per ~3s AND >=12 files since the last edit (progress.js documents Telegram's ~1 edit/s/chat limit; the copy loop emits once per 4 files, i.e. ~1/s, so the throttle cuts edit volume ~12x), with the terminal copy-complete event always rendered. Reporting is best-effort: a throwing callback cannot break the clone (verified). Error/success paths unchanged (renderFreshView error view / success sendMessage + showHome). VERIFIED end-to-end against the live GitHub API: a real clone creation emitted 79 well-formed events — source(done 0/302) once, copy 77 times strictly monotonic 4..302/302, finalize(302/302) once — and a deliberately throwing callback on the first event did not affect the clone (302 files, repo cleaned up after). Bot test suite: 110/110 pass. Fix commit a650209.
